articles.title: Ian Garry Just Screwed Michael Morales
articles.description: Michael Morales appears to be in position for a title fight with Islam Makhachev, but Chael Sonnen believes Ian Machado Garry may have just changed everything without throwing a punch. Garry publicly called for a fight with Morales. Morales hasn't responded. And according to Chael, that's exactly the problem. At the same time, Prates is actively making his case for the title opportunity while Morales has done surprisingly little publicly to secure his position. If Garry's challenge becomes accepted as the obvious next fight for Morales, Prates could suddenly be the last man standing for Islam. Chael compares it to previous UFC title races where one contender effectively removed both himself and a rival by calling for a fight, leaving someone else alone at the front of the line. Morales may still get Islam next. But until the bout agreement is signed, Chael argues his team cannot allow someone else to control the narrative. Ian Garry called him out. Now Michael Morales has a problem. articles.title: Give Ilia his REMATCH!
articles.description: The resistance to an immediate rematch between Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje has surprised Chael Sonnen. Topuria entered their first fight undefeated, as a former featherweight champion, lightweight champion and the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in the world. He was also a significant favorite before Gaethje pulled off the upset. Now some are arguing that Topuria needs to rebuild before getting another opportunity. Chael doesn't buy it. Historically, champions in Topuria's position have received immediate rematches, particularly after a stoppage. And if the argument against Gaethje is about protecting Topuria, Chael points out another problem: the supposed "safer" alternatives include fighters like Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira, both of whom have already beaten Gaethje. Meanwhile, Arman Tsarukyan, Mauricio Ruffy and others are still sorting out their own positions in the lightweight title picture. For Chael, the matchmaking question isn't how the UFC could justify Topuria vs. Gaethje 2. It's what argument justifies denying it. Ilia Topuria has earned the right to get his belt back. articles.title: Max Holloway MUST Accept the Fight
articles.description: Parnassé is only 1-0 in the UFC, but after finishing Dan Hooker in a main event, he wasted no time calling out Max Holloway. Chael Sonnen isn't predicting that the UFC will actually make the fight. He's making a different argument: Max has to accept the challenge. Holloway is the BMF. He's the guy who points to the center of the Octagon and invites opponents to trade. When someone publicly calls that guy out, especially after a performance like Parnassé just delivered, Chael believes Max can't simply ignore it. And Max may have accidentally put himself in this position. After his fight with Conor McGregor, Holloway called for another fight with Conor even though McGregor isn't currently available. Had Max been publicly attached to Arman Tsarukyan, Mauricio Ruffy or another active contender, Parnassé might never have called his name. Instead, Max looked available. Parnassé saw the opening and took it. The UFC doesn't have to book the fight. But according to Chael, Max Holloway has to accept the challenge. articles.title: Khabib Nurmagomedov tries to wrestle Chael Sonnen #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen explains why what Nurmagomedov did inside the cage wasn’t a surprise. If you’ve watched enough fighters from that system, Chael says you start to recognize the pattern: strike just enough to close the distance, get into the clinch, lock up the body, and work toward the takedown. And that creates a major problem. Fighting is built around surprise. But the more footage you have on an opponent, the less surprising their tendencies become. Chael believes that’s especially important at the highest level of MMA. A top fighter who understands the game can study an opponent long enough to identify the patterns, anticipate what’s coming, and take away the element of surprise. The question is simple: How predictable is too predictable? Because once an elite fighter knows what you want to do before you do it, the entire fight can change. #MMA #UFC #ChaelSonnen #Nurmagomedov #Khabib #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews #MMAFighting #FightBreakdown

articles.title: Is Arman vs. Ruffy Really a No. 1 Contender Fight? #ufc
articles.description: If Arman Tsarukyan vs. Ruffy is a No. 1 contender fight, then the UFC needs to treat it like one. Chael Sonnen was told that this five-round co-main event was elevated specifically because of what’s at stake: the winner takes the next step toward the lightweight title and could face Justin Gaethje for the belt. That makes sense. But there’s a problem. Just yesterday, Chael made the case that Charles Oliveira or Max Holloway could potentially be next for the title. So which is it? You can’t keep calling fights “No. 1 contender” bouts if the winner isn’t actually guaranteed the next opportunity. Chael argues that MMA has never done a good enough job demanding clarity when it comes to title contention. If you announce a No. 1 contender fight, there should be one simple understanding: The winner gets the title shot. So if Arman Tsarukyan and Ruffy are fighting for that position, let's make the stakes official. No confusion. No moving the goalposts. No picking someone else afterward. #ArmanTsarukyan #Ruffy #UFC #MMA #JustinGaethje #UFCNews #ChaelSonnen #MMAAnalysis #Lightweight

articles.title: 🚨 Dana White says the heavyweight division isn't waiting around for Tom Aspinall
articles.description: Dana White says Tom Aspinall IS coming back — but only when he’s healthy and medically ready. 👀🔥 The UFC heavyweight champion has been sidelined since suffering a serious eye injury against Ciryl Gane at UFC 321 in October 2025, ultimately requiring multiple surgeries. With speculation growing about Aspinall’s future, Dana shut down talk that he could be leaving the UFC: 🗣️ “He’s not going anywhere. He’s with us, and we’re good with Tom Aspinall.” White says the timeline is straightforward: when Aspinall is healthy and ready, he’ll fight again. Aspinall has also publicly confirmed that he has no intention of leaving the UFC. articles.title: Ian Garry Has a New Target: Michael Morales #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry has a new target — Michael Morales. After his fight with Islam Makhachev, Garry has looked at the landscape and apparently decided that if he can't get the immediate rematch or another title opportunity, he's going after the next-best option. And Chael Sonnen thinks there may be some serious logic behind it. Garry and Morales have history, including a memorable backstage interaction where Garry kept asking Morales, “Does that make sense?” while Morales politely tried to follow along. Now they're potentially on a collision course. According to Chael, Garry is looking at the entire board and making a calculated move. If Dana White is right that Garry may have difficulty getting another championship opportunity, then the fastest way back to the title picture may be beating the guy who could be next in line. Ian Garry vs. Michael Morales. A win over Morales could change everything. #IanGarry #MichaelMorales #UFC #MMA #IslamMakhachev #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #Welterweight

articles.title: Stop Pretending Gaethje vs. Ilia 2 Is Next
articles.description: Can we stop pretending Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria 2 is automatically next? Chael believes Gaethje’s next fight could be his last—and Justin has already made one thing clear: if that’s the case, he wants someone new. That’s where Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy come in. If their five-round fight is truly a No. 1 contender matchup, Chael argues the UFC should treat it like one. Let them fight, let a new challenger emerge, and give the winner something meaningful. With Gaethje unlikely to compete again until next year anyway, the timing could line up perfectly. Chael also explains why he doesn’t hate the idea of Topuria-Gaethje 2. Their first fight was far more competitive than the ending suggests. But if Gaethje is really preparing for one final fight, an immediate rematch creates another problem: an Ilia victory leaves them 1-1 with no guarantee the trilogy ever happens. There’s new blood coming at lightweight. There’s a potential No. 1 contender fight already on the calendar. And Gaethje wants a new opponent. Chael thinks the answer may already be sitting right in front of us. articles.title: Alex Pereira Deserves a Rematch?
articles.description: The UFC heavyweight division has two champions, Tom Aspinall’s return remains unclear, Ciryl Gane and Alex Pereira continue to be discussed for an immediate rematch and Josh Hokit is sitting there wondering why he’s the one without a fight. Chael breaks down the increasingly complicated heavyweight picture and why Hokit has a legitimate argument. If Aspinall isn’t available yet, the interim championship needs to mean something. Gane can defend it. Pereira needs an opponent. And Hokit has already publicly called out both men. There’s also conflicting information surrounding Aspinall’s recovery. Eddie Hearn says Tom is back training at full speed, while people around Aspinall have offered very different accounts. Chael explains why Hokit immediately seized on those comments and why the distinction between training and being medically cleared matters. But ultimately, this isn’t about Aspinall’s injury. It’s about keeping the heavyweight division moving. Hokit is healthy. He’s ready. He wants a champion. And right now, the UFC happens to have two of them. articles.title: Pay Attention to Ian Garry!
articles.description: Ian Garry could have come out after his loss with the same message we hear from every fighter: thank the team, thank the fans, mention an injury without really explaining it, promise to come back stronger. Instead, Garry gave us something useful. He called out Michael Morales. Chael explains why that might be a much smarter move than it initially appears. If Islam Makhachev’s next welterweight title defense is already headed toward Carlos Prates, Garry needs another way to move himself toward the front of the line. Morales is undefeated, dangerous, and sitting ahead of him in the division. Beating him would mean something. There’s also Shavkat Rakhmonov waiting to return, Dana White’s lack of interest in another Garry-Islam fight, and the reality that Garry may need to take a much harder road back to a championship opportunity than another contender would. But Garry appears willing to do exactly that. Chael breaks down the chess move behind the Morales callout—and why Garry may have walked away from his last fight realizing something important about himself: he’s better than he thought he was. articles.title: I’d Kick That Gorilla Right in the Nuts #ufc
articles.description: Could Chael Sonnen take on a silverback gorilla? According to Chael, he's got a plan. The conversation starts with Mark Schultz and the famous story of choking out a bear — but there's one important detail that changes everything. The bear had a muzzle. And its paws were covered. So, maybe it wasn't exactly a fight to the death. But when the conversation turns to the legendary 100 men versus one gorilla debate, Chael doesn't hesitate. Everyone talks about the gorilla's strength. Chael has other ideas. Eye pokes. Low blows. Anything goes. Chael explains exactly how he would approach a silverback gorilla — and let's just say his confidence remains completely intact. Would Chael and 100 of his friends actually stand a chance? Chael Sonnen seems to think so. #ChaelSonnen #Gorilla #MMA #Funny #SilverbackGorilla #Comedy #MarkSchultz #UFC #ChaelSonnenPodcast

articles.title: Chimaev’s Next Fight Just Got Interesting #ufc
articles.description: Khamzat Chimaev called out Sean Strickland — but then he pivoted. If Sean isn't next, Chimaev named three potential opponents: Nassourdine Imavov, Caio Borralho, or Dricus Du Plessis. But Chael Sonnen sees some problems. Dricus? They just fought. Imavov? That's an interesting option — but if Chimaev gets Imavov, then who does Sean Strickland fight? And then there's Caio Borralho. Chael is all in. Caio Borralho vs. Khamzat Chimaev is a matchup Chael would watch all day. But more importantly, it could solve Chimaev's biggest problem: proving that Sean Strickland is the only fight left. Because that's what Chael believes Chimaev is really doing. He's not abandoning the Strickland fight. He's saying, if you need me to fight someone first, bring me the opponent. Win that fight, and Chimaev vs. Strickland is no longer a callout. It's the fight that has to happen. #KhamzatChimaev #SeanStrickland #CaioBorralho #NassourdineImavov #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis
